# splitsecure_connected_app (Resource)

Connected app in a SplitSecure vault, built from a catalog template and bound to a SAML2 identity provider or an OIDC issuer. Creating or deleting it may need approval, and the call waits for it. Changing the folder moves the record in place. Changing any other input replaces the resource.

## Example Usage

From the [`aws-saml`](https://github.com/splitsecure/terraform-provider-splitsecure/tree/main/examples/aws-saml) scenario:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {
      source = "splitsecure/splitsecure"
    }
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = ">= 5.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

provider "aws" {
  region = var.aws_region
}

data "splitsecure_vault" "aws_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

data "aws_iam_policy" "read_only_access" {
  name = "ReadOnlyAccess"
}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "aws" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The identity provider that signs every SAML assertion.
resource "splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider" "aws_console" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.aws.id
  name      = "AWS console sign-in"

  justification = "Sign in to the AWS console with SAML"
}

# AWS trusts the identity provider through its metadata.
resource "aws_iam_saml_provider" "splitsecure" {
  name                   = "SplitSecure"
  saml_metadata_document = splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider.aws_console.metadata_xml
}

# The app carries principal tags, so the trust policy allows sts:TagSession.
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "assume_with_saml" {
  statement {
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML", "sts:TagSession"]

    principals {
      type        = "Federated"
      identifiers = [aws_iam_saml_provider.splitsecure.arn]
    }

    condition {
      test     = "StringEquals"
      variable = "SAML:aud"
      values   = ["https://signin.aws.amazon.com/saml"]
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "console_read_only" {
  name                 = var.role_name
  assume_role_policy   = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume_with_saml.json
  max_session_duration = 3600
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "console_read_only" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.console_read_only.name
  policy_arn = data.aws_iam_policy.read_only_access.arn
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "aws_console" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider.aws_console.id
  template        = "saml2/aws"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.aws.id
  name            = "AWS console (${var.role_name})"

  saml2 {
    entity_id = "urn:amazon:webservices"
    acs_url   = "https://signin.aws.amazon.com/saml"
  }

  field {
    name  = "role_arn"
    value = aws_iam_role.console_read_only.arn
  }

  field {
    name  = "saml_provider_arn"
    value = aws_iam_saml_provider.splitsecure.arn
  }

  # The NameID is the requester's email.
  field {
    name  = "name_id_format"
    value = "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress"
  }

  field {
    name      = "requester_email"
    requester = "email"
  }

  name_id {
    parts = ["field:requester_email"]
  }

  # Each sign-in chooses a session length up to the role's maximum.
  field {
    name = "session_duration"
    duration_range {
      min_seconds     = 900
      max_seconds     = aws_iam_role.console_read_only.max_session_duration
      default_seconds = 1800
    }
  }

  field {
    name  = "session_tag"
    key   = "Team"
    value = var.team_tag
  }

  justification = "Let the team sign in to the ${var.role_name} role"
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.aws_console.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

From the [`aws-oidc`](https://github.com/splitsecure/terraform-provider-splitsecure/tree/main/examples/aws-oidc) scenario:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {
      source = "splitsecure/splitsecure"
    }
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = ">= 5.0"
    }
    tls = {
      source  = "hashicorp/tls"
      version = ">= 4.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

provider "aws" {
  region = var.aws_region
}

data "splitsecure_vault" "aws_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

data "aws_caller_identity" "current" {}

data "aws_partition" "current" {}

data "aws_iam_policy" "read_only_access" {
  name = "ReadOnlyAccess"
}

locals {
  # The app names the role before the role exists: its trust policy needs the app's subject.
  role_arn = "arn:${data.aws_partition.current.partition}:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:role/${var.role_name}"

  # AWS keys the provider's condition keys by the issuer URL without its scheme.
  issuer_host = trimprefix(splitsecure_oidc_issuer.aws_federation.issuer, "https://")
}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "aws" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The issuer that signs every token. AWS takes ES256 and ES384 keys.
resource "splitsecure_oidc_issuer" "aws_federation" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.aws.id
  name      = "AWS federation issuer"
  algs      = ["ES256"]

  justification = "Issue tokens AWS exchanges for role sessions"
}

data "tls_certificate" "issuer" {
  url = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.aws_federation.issuer
}

resource "aws_iam_openid_connect_provider" "splitsecure" {
  url             = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.aws_federation.issuer
  client_id_list  = ["sts.amazonaws.com"]
  thumbprint_list = [data.tls_certificate.issuer.certificates[0].sha1_fingerprint]
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "aws_session" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.aws_federation.id
  template        = "oidc/aws"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.aws.id
  name            = "AWS role session (${var.role_name})"

  oidc {
    key_id = one([for k in splitsecure_oidc_issuer.aws_federation.keys : k.key_id if k.alg == "ES256"])
  }

  field {
    name  = "role_arn"
    value = local.role_arn
  }

  # Each sign-in chooses a session length up to the role's maximum.
  field {
    name = "session_duration"
    duration_range {
      min_seconds     = 900
      max_seconds     = var.max_session_seconds
      default_seconds = 1800
    }
  }

  field {
    name  = "session_tag"
    key   = "Team"
    value = var.team_tag
  }

  justification = "Let the team sign in to the ${var.role_name} role"
}

# Every token carries principal tags and the requester's session name as the
# source identity, so the trust policy allows sts:TagSession and
# sts:SetSourceIdentity. The subject is the one the enclave derived for this app.
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "assume_with_token" {
  statement {
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity", "sts:TagSession", "sts:SetSourceIdentity"]

    principals {
      type        = "Federated"
      identifiers = [aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.splitsecure.arn]
    }

    condition {
      test     = "StringEquals"
      variable = "${local.issuer_host}:aud"
      values   = ["sts.amazonaws.com"]
    }

    condition {
      test     = "StringEquals"
      variable = "${local.issuer_host}:sub"
      values   = [splitsecure_connected_app.aws_session.derived_values["subject"]]
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "session_read_only" {
  name                 = var.role_name
  assume_role_policy   = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume_with_token.json
  max_session_duration = var.max_session_seconds
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "session_read_only" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.session_read_only.name
  policy_arn = data.aws_iam_policy.read_only_access.arn
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.aws_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.aws_session.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

From the [`gcp-saml`](https://github.com/splitsecure/terraform-provider-splitsecure/tree/main/examples/gcp-saml) scenario:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {
      source = "splitsecure/splitsecure"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = ">= 6.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

provider "google" {
  project = var.project_id
}

data "splitsecure_vault" "gcp_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

locals {
  pool_path = "locations/global/workforcePools/${google_iam_workforce_pool.splitsecure.workforce_pool_id}"

  # Google Cloud names the service provider by the pool and the provider.
  provider_path = "${local.pool_path}/providers/${google_iam_workforce_pool_provider.splitsecure.provider_id}"
}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "gcp" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The identity provider that signs every SAML assertion.
resource "splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider" "gcp_console" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.gcp.id
  name      = "Google Cloud console sign-in"

  justification = "Sign in to the Google Cloud console with SAML"
}

# A workforce pool of the organization, for people outside Google's own directory.
resource "google_iam_workforce_pool" "splitsecure" {
  parent            = "organizations/${var.organization_id}"
  location          = "global"
  workforce_pool_id = var.pool_id
  display_name      = "SplitSecure"
  session_duration  = "3600s"
}

# The pool trusts the identity provider through its metadata, and takes the NameID as the user.
resource "google_iam_workforce_pool_provider" "splitsecure" {
  workforce_pool_id = google_iam_workforce_pool.splitsecure.workforce_pool_id
  location          = google_iam_workforce_pool.splitsecure.location
  provider_id       = var.pool_provider_id
  display_name      = "SplitSecure"

  attribute_mapping = {
    "google.subject" = "assertion.subject"
  }

  saml {
    idp_metadata_xml = splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider.gcp_console.metadata_xml
  }
}

# Each user gets the role on the project. The subject is the NameID: the requester's email.
resource "google_project_iam_member" "federated_user" {
  for_each = toset(var.user_emails)

  project = var.project_id
  role    = var.user_role
  member  = "principal://iam.googleapis.com/${local.pool_path}/subject/${each.value}"
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "gcp_console" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider.gcp_console.id
  template        = "saml2/gcp"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.gcp.id
  name            = "Google Cloud console (${var.pool_id})"

  saml2 {
    entity_id = "https://iam.googleapis.com/${local.provider_path}"
    acs_url   = "https://auth.cloud.google/signin-callback/${local.provider_path}"
  }

  # The NameID is the requester's email.
  field {
    name  = "name_id_format"
    value = "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress"
  }

  field {
    name      = "requester_email"
    requester = "email"
  }

  name_id {
    parts = ["field:requester_email"]
  }

  justification = "Let the team sign in to the Google Cloud console"
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.gcp_console.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

From the [`gcp-oidc`](https://github.com/splitsecure/terraform-provider-splitsecure/tree/main/examples/gcp-oidc) scenario:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {
      source = "splitsecure/splitsecure"
    }
    google = {
      source  = "hashicorp/google"
      version = ">= 6.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

provider "google" {
  project = var.project_id
}

data "splitsecure_vault" "gcp_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

data "google_project" "current" {}

locals {
  pool_name = "projects/${data.google_project.current.number}/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool.splitsecure.workload_identity_pool_id}"

  # The audience every token carries: the full name of the pool provider.
  audience = "https://iam.googleapis.com/${local.pool_name}/providers/${google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider.splitsecure.workload_identity_pool_provider_id}"
}

# The token exchange and the service account impersonation need these APIs.
resource "google_project_service" "federation" {
  for_each = toset(["iam.googleapis.com", "iamcredentials.googleapis.com", "sts.googleapis.com"])

  service            = each.value
  disable_on_destroy = false
}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "gcp" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The issuer that signs every token. Google Cloud takes an ES256 key.
resource "splitsecure_oidc_issuer" "gcp_federation" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.gcp.id
  name      = "Google Cloud federation issuer"
  algs      = ["ES256"]

  justification = "Issue tokens Google Cloud exchanges for service account tokens"
}

resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool" "splitsecure" {
  workload_identity_pool_id = var.pool_id
  display_name              = "SplitSecure"

  depends_on = [google_project_service.federation]
}

# The pool provider trusts the issuer, takes the audience of its own name, and maps the token subject.
resource "google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider" "splitsecure" {
  workload_identity_pool_id          = google_iam_workload_identity_pool.splitsecure.workload_identity_pool_id
  workload_identity_pool_provider_id = var.pool_provider_id
  display_name                       = "SplitSecure issuer"

  attribute_mapping = {
    "google.subject" = "assertion.sub"
  }

  oidc {
    issuer_uri        = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.gcp_federation.issuer
    allowed_audiences = ["https://iam.googleapis.com/${local.pool_name}/providers/${var.pool_provider_id}"]
  }
}

# The service account a token is exchanged for.
resource "google_service_account" "federated" {
  account_id   = var.service_account_id
  display_name = "SplitSecure federated access"
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "federated" {
  project = var.project_id
  role    = var.service_account_role
  member  = google_service_account.federated.member
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "gcp_service_account" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.gcp_federation.id
  template        = "oidc/gcp"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.gcp.id
  name            = "Google Cloud (${var.service_account_id})"

  oidc {
    key_id = one([for k in splitsecure_oidc_issuer.gcp_federation.keys : k.key_id if k.alg == "ES256"])
  }

  field {
    name  = "project_number"
    value = data.google_project.current.number
  }

  field {
    name  = "pool_id"
    value = google_iam_workload_identity_pool.splitsecure.workload_identity_pool_id
  }

  field {
    name  = "provider_id"
    value = google_iam_workload_identity_pool_provider.splitsecure.workload_identity_pool_provider_id
  }

  field {
    name  = "service_account_email"
    value = google_service_account.federated.email
  }

  # Each sign-in chooses how long the service account token lives.
  field {
    name = "access_token_lifetime"
    duration_range {
      min_seconds     = 300
      max_seconds     = 3600
      default_seconds = 3600
    }
  }

  justification = "Let the team act as ${var.service_account_id}"
}

# Only tokens with the subject SplitSecure derived for this app can act as the service account.
resource "google_service_account_iam_member" "token_exchange" {
  service_account_id = google_service_account.federated.name
  role               = "roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser"
  member             = "principal://iam.googleapis.com/${local.pool_name}/subject/${splitsecure_connected_app.gcp_service_account.derived_values["subject"]}"
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.gcp_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.gcp_service_account.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

From the [`azure-saml`](https://github.com/splitsecure/terraform-provider-splitsecure/tree/main/examples/azure-saml) scenario:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {
      source = "splitsecure/splitsecure"
    }
    azuread = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azuread"
      version = ">= 3.0"
    }
    random = {
      source  = "hashicorp/random"
      version = ">= 3.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

# Reads the tenant and the credentials from the Azure CLI or the ARM_ environment variables.
provider "azuread" {}

data "splitsecure_vault" "azure_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

# The verified domains of the tenant.
data "azuread_domains" "verified" {}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "azure" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The identity provider that signs every SAML assertion. Entra ID trusts it once the domain is federated.
resource "splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider" "entra_domain" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.azure.id
  name      = "Entra ID sign-in (${var.domain})"

  justification = "Sign in to Entra ID with SAML for ${var.domain}"
}

# Entra ID finds a federated user by the immutable id in the NameID.
resource "random_uuid" "immutable_id" {}

# Entra ID needs a password to create the user. Federated sign-in does not use it.
resource "random_password" "unused" {
  length  = 32
  special = true
}

resource "azuread_user" "federated" {
  user_principal_name     = "${var.user_name}@${var.domain}"
  display_name            = var.display_name
  mail_nickname           = var.user_name
  onpremises_immutable_id = random_uuid.immutable_id.result
  password                = random_password.unused.result

  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = contains([for d in data.azuread_domains.verified.domains : d.domain_name], var.domain)
      error_message = "The domain is not a verified domain of the tenant. Add and verify it in Entra ID first."
    }
  }
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "entra_user" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_saml2_identity_provider.entra_domain.id
  template        = "saml2/microsoft-entra-id"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.azure.id
  name            = "Entra ID (${azuread_user.federated.user_principal_name})"

  # The service provider values from Microsoft's federation metadata.
  saml2 {
    entity_id = "urn:federation:MicrosoftOnline"
    acs_url   = "https://login.microsoftonline.com/login.srf"
  }

  # A persistent NameID that holds the user's immutable id.
  field {
    name  = "name_id_format"
    value = "urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:nameid-format:persistent"
  }

  field {
    name  = "name_id"
    value = azuread_user.federated.onpremises_immutable_id
  }

  field {
    name  = "user_principal_name"
    value = azuread_user.federated.user_principal_name
  }

  justification = "Let the team sign in to Entra ID as ${azuread_user.federated.user_principal_name}"
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.entra_user.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

```terraform
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    splitsecure = {

    }
    azuread = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azuread"
      version = ">= 3.0"
    }
  }
}

# Reads SPLITSECURE_ORG_S2R, SPLITSECURE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_S2R, SPLITSECURE_KEY_ID
# and SPLITSECURE_PRIVATE_KEY, and SPLITSECURE_ENDPOINT outside production.
provider "splitsecure" {}

# Reads the tenant and the credentials from the Azure CLI or the ARM_ environment variables.
provider "azuread" {}

data "splitsecure_vault" "azure_access" {
  name = var.vault_name
}

data "azuread_client_config" "current" {}

# The folder that holds the records. Deleting it moves anything left inside to lost+found.
resource "splitsecure_vault_folder" "azure" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  name      = var.folder_name
  parent_id = var.parent_folder_id == "" ? null : var.parent_folder_id
}

# The issuer that signs every token. Entra ID takes an RS256 key only.
resource "splitsecure_oidc_issuer" "entra_federation" {
  vault_id  = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  folder_id = splitsecure_vault_folder.azure.id
  name      = "Entra ID federation issuer"
  algs      = ["RS256"]

  justification = "Issue tokens Entra ID exchanges for application tokens"
}

# The application a token signs in as, and its service principal in the tenant.
resource "azuread_application" "federated" {
  display_name = var.application_name
}

resource "azuread_service_principal" "federated" {
  client_id = azuread_application.federated.client_id
}

resource "splitsecure_connected_app" "entra_application" {
  issuer_vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  issuer_id       = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.entra_federation.id
  template        = "oidc/azure"
  folder_id       = splitsecure_vault_folder.azure.id
  name            = "Entra ID (${var.application_name})"

  oidc {
    key_id = one([for k in splitsecure_oidc_issuer.entra_federation.keys : k.key_id if k.alg == "RS256"])
  }

  field {
    name  = "tenant_id"
    value = data.azuread_client_config.current.tenant_id
  }

  field {
    name  = "client_id"
    value = azuread_application.federated.client_id
  }

  # Each sign-in chooses how long the token lives.
  field {
    name = "lifetime"
    duration_range {
      min_seconds     = 300
      max_seconds     = 3600
      default_seconds = 600
    }
  }

  justification = "Let the team sign in as ${var.application_name}"
}

# Entra ID accepts a token whose issuer, subject and audience match this credential.
resource "azuread_application_federated_identity_credential" "splitsecure" {
  application_id = azuread_application.federated.id
  display_name   = "splitsecure"
  issuer         = splitsecure_oidc_issuer.entra_federation.issuer
  subject        = splitsecure_connected_app.entra_application.derived_values["subject"]
  audiences      = ["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]
}

# Optional: let a principal or group use the app.
resource "splitsecure_vault_grant" "app_use" {
  count = var.grantee == "" ? 0 : 1

  vault_id = data.splitsecure_vault.azure_access.id
  node_id  = splitsecure_connected_app.entra_application.id
  grantee  = var.grantee
  tier     = "use"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `issuer_id` (String) Id of the SAML2 identity provider or OIDC issuer record that signs for the app. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `issuer_vault_id` (String) Vault of the issuer record. The app is created in it. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `name` (String) Human-readable name. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `template` (String) Catalog template the app is built from, such as saml2/aws or oidc/aws. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `description` (String) Free-form description. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `field` (Block List) One field of the template. Set exactly one of value, values, seconds, duration_range, choices or affix with its default, requester, derived and json. The order of the field blocks does not matter. Changing any field replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--field))
- `folder` (List of String) Folder path from the vault root to place the connected app in, for example ["terraform", "prod"]. Missing folders are created. Unset places it at the vault root. Changing it moves the record.
- `folder_id` (String) Node id of an existing folder to place the connected app in, such as the id of a splitsecure_vault_folder. Set at most one of folder and folder_id. Changing it moves the record.
- `justification` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Justification shown to approvers when the create needs approval. Write-only and never stored in state.
- `name_id` (Block List) NameID of a SAML2 app, built from parts. Replaces the template's name_id field wherever the layout places it. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--name_id))
- `notification_policy` (String) Who is notified about requests against the connected app. One of: notify_everyone, allow_selective_notifications. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `oidc` (Block List) Signing key of an OIDC template. Set this block or saml2, not both. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--oidc))
- `saml2` (Block List) Service provider of a SAML2 template: entity_id and acs_url, or its metadata_xml. Set this block or oidc, not both. Changing it replaces the resource. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--saml2))
- `sensitivity` (String) Sensitivity level of the connected app. One of: low, medium, high, critical. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `wait` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) How long the server holds the create open for approval before Terraform starts polling, as a Go duration such as "30s". Defaults to 0. Write-only and never stored in state.

### Read-Only

- `derived_values` (Map of String) Values the enclave derived when it created the app, by field name. For oidc/aws, subject is the sub claim the role's trust policy must match.
- `id` (String) Record id in the vault. Also the import id as vault_id/id.
- `title` (String) Display name of the template.
- `vault_id` (String) Vault the connected app lives in, the vault of its issuer.

<a id="nestedblock--field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `field`

Required:

- `name` (String) Field name as the template declares it, such as role_arn.

Optional:

- `affix` (Block List) Text each sign-in sets within a prefix, a suffix and a length, for a text field. Set it in place of choices. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--field--affix))
- `choices` (List of String) Values each sign-in chooses from: one for a text field, any of them for a list field. Defaults to the template's choices for the field.
- `default_value` (String) Value a sign-in gets when it sets none, for a text field with choices or affix.
- `default_values` (List of String) Choices a sign-in gets when it chooses none, for a list field.
- `derived` (String) Text the enclave derives: at_creation or per_sign_in.
- `duration_range` (Block List) Duration each sign-in chooses within bounds, in seconds. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--field--duration_range))
- `json` (String) Fixed JSON object, such as jsonencode({team = "platform"}). Numbers must be integers.
- `key` (String) Marks the entry as an instance of a repeatable field, carried under this key: a session tag key, a claim name or an attribute name.
- `requester` (String) Text filled from the requester: email or session_name.
- `seconds` (Number) Fixed duration in seconds.
- `suffix` (String) Ending a requester value must have, such as @corp.example.
- `value` (String) Fixed text.
- `values` (List of String) Fixed list of text.

<a id="nestedblock--field--affix"></a>
### Nested Schema for `field.affix`

Optional:

- `max_length` (Number) Most bytes the value may have. Unset or 0 sets no limit.
- `prefix` (String) Beginning the value must have.
- `suffix` (String) Ending the value must have.


<a id="nestedblock--field--duration_range"></a>
### Nested Schema for `field.duration_range`

Required:

- `max_seconds` (Number) Longest duration a sign-in may choose.
- `min_seconds` (Number) Shortest duration a sign-in may choose.

Optional:

- `default_seconds` (Number) Duration a sign-in gets when it chooses none.



<a id="nestedblock--name_id"></a>
### Nested Schema for `name_id`

Required:

- `parts` (List of String) Parts joined in order. A part starting with field: is the value of the named field; any other part is literal text.


<a id="nestedblock--oidc"></a>
### Nested Schema for `oidc`

Required:

- `key_id` (String) Base64 vault key id of the issuer key that signs tokens, as the issuer's keys export it.


<a id="nestedblock--saml2"></a>
### Nested Schema for `saml2`

Optional:

- `acs_url` (String) Assertion consumer service URL, posted to with HTTP-POST. Set it with entity_id.
- `entity_id` (String) Entity id of the service provider, the assertion audience. Set it with acs_url.
- `metadata_xml` (String) SAML 2.0 metadata of the service provider: one EntityDescriptor. Set it in place of entity_id and acs_url. Formatting changes that keep the same metadata are not a change.
